questions.subject: English Language
questions.question: Neither the principal nor the vice-principals _______ aware of the sudden change in the examination timetable.
questions.explanation: By the rule of proximity concord, when two subjects are joined by 'neither... nor', the verb agrees in number and person with the noun closer to it ('vice-principals', which is plural). Hence, 'were' is correct.
questions.explanation_short: Proximity concord: plural verb 'were' agrees with 'vice-principals'.
questions.explanation_pidgin: For 'neither... nor', the verb dey follow the subject wey near am pass. Since 'vice-principals' na plural, we use 'were'.

questions.subject: English Language
questions.question: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in italics: The auditor discovered a *flagrant* breach of financial regulations.
questions.explanation: 'Flagrant' describes an offense or error that is conspicuously bad, obvious, or glaring.
questions.explanation_pidgin: 'Flagrant' mean say the mistake or offense open-eye well-well, e no hide at all — so 'glaring' correct.
